> **Python user?** The Python package has the same functions and arguments;
> R's `verb(m, ...)` is `m.verb(...)` there. See the
> [Python documentation](../../python/).

basemapper renders MapLibre GL basemaps headlessly with a Rust core: no
browser, display server, GPU or GDAL. Vector styles are drawn by a software
port of MapLibre GL JS's renderer, so maps look as they do in MapLibre.

## Installation

```r
remotes::install_github("ar-puuk/basemapper", subdir = "r-basemapper")
```

## Step 1 — Choose a style

Every function takes a `style`: a MapLibre GL style URL or JSON string, or a
vector of styles stacked bottom to top. `basemap_provider()` names 25 common
basemaps; the other providers build styles for tile services:

```r
library(basemapper)

list_providers()
positron <- basemap_provider("Carto.Positron")

# XYZ raster tiles
osm <- raster_provider("https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png")

# An ArcGIS vector tile service's published style
esri <- esri_vector_provider(
  "https://basemaps.arcgis.com/arcgis/rest/services/World_Basemap_v2/VectorTileServer"
)

# One layer of an MVT source, with paint overrides
mvt <- vector_provider(
  "https://example.com/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.mvt", source_layer = "land",
  paint = list("fill-color" = "#e8e0d8", "line-color" = "#aaaaaa")
)
```

`list_layers()` lists a style's layers (id and type) in drawing order:

```r
list_layers(positron)
```

## Step 2 — A map on its own

`basemap()` creates a view: a centre and MapLibre zoom, or bounds to fit.
`width` and `height` are CSS pixels; `pixel_ratio` makes the image larger
with the same view and label layout (`pixel_ratio = 2` for a sharp 2x image,
`dpi / 96` for print).

```r
m <- basemap(positron, 800, 600, center = c(-111.8887, 40.7556), zoom = 12.4,
             pixel_ratio = 2)
m
#> <basemap> 1 style, 800 x 600 @ 2x (1600 x 1200 px), center (-111.88870, 40.75560), zoom 12.400

render_png(m, path = "slc.png")
render_svg(m, path = "slc.svg")   # true vector, labels as editable text
r <- render_raster(m)             # terra SpatRaster in EPSG:3857
a <- render_array(m)              # [1200, 1600, 4] integer array
```

Change the view with `set_view()` and `set_bounds()`, and read it with
`get_bounds()`, `get_center()`, `get_zoom()` and `get_size()`:

```r
nc <- sf::st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)
m <- set_bounds(m, nc)            # fit an sf object's extent
get_zoom(m)
get_bounds(m, lonlat = TRUE)
m <- set_view(m, zoom = get_zoom(m) + 1)
```

## Step 3 — Render with {ggplot2}

`geom_basemap()` renders when the plot is drawn, for the panel's extent and
at the device's resolution, so `ggsave(dpi = 300)` gets a basemap rendered at
300 dpi:

```r
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(nc) +
  geom_basemap(positron) +
  geom_sf(fill = NA, colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.4) +
  coord_sf() +
  theme_void()
```

## Step 4 — Render with {tmap}

`tm_basemap()` is a {tmap} v4 element that takes its extent from the active
`tm_shape()`:

```r
library(tmap)

tm_shape(nc) +
  tm_basemap(positron) +
  tm_borders(col = "steelblue")
```

The plot layers share these arguments (in Python too):

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `style` | — | Style URL / JSON, or a vector stacked bottom to top |
| `tile_zoom` | `NULL` (as MapLibre) | Tile detail override on the 256 px grid |
| `alpha` | `1` | Basemap opacity |
| `layers` | `NULL` (all) | Layer filter — see below |
| `pixel_ratio` | device dpi / 96 | Device pixels per CSS pixel |
| `auth_token` | `NULL` | Access token for the tile service |
| `tile_timeout_ms` | `10000` | Per-tile HTTP timeout |
| `max_tiles` | `256` | Cap on tiles fetched per style |

## Step 5 — Filter layers

Pass layer IDs to `layers` to keep only those layers, or prefix IDs with
`"-"` to drop them. Keeping and dropping cannot be mixed.

```r
# Without town and village labels
render_png(basemap(positron, 800, 600, bounds = nc, layers = c("-place_town", "-place_villages")),
           path = "nc.png")

ggplot(nc) + geom_basemap(positron, layers = c("background", "water"))
```

## Step 6 — One-shot rendering

`render_basemap_raw()` renders bounds in one call and returns the pixels with
their extent, for custom compositing or export:

```r
a <- render_basemap_raw(nc, 800, 600, positron)

dim(a)                # 600 800 4
attr(a, "crs_epsg")   # 4267, the CRS of `nc`
png::writePNG(a / 255, "basemap.png")
```
